sampling_model.design: Randomized finite-arm instrument with \(\lambda_z=P(Z=z)>0\) for every population arm, with inference conditional on the realized positive arm counts \((n_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units from a law in \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal T,\mathcal C}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The realized exposure lies in \(\mathcal X=\mathcal T\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal C\); target levels obey exclusion and off-target levels have saturated arm-specific responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Population positivity \(\lambda_z>0\) defines every conditional arm law \(p_z\) and skeleton law \(s_z\). The separate realized-sample condition \(n_z\ge1\) is required for finite-sample calibration; positive limiting arm proportions and an interior skeleton are used solely for the regular-face lower bound.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated: conditional on fixed finite arm counts, off-target allocations \(\eta_z\) factor variation-independently, induce finite-fiber kernels \(K_\eta(\nu\mid\sigma)\), and are removed before KL calibration.

body.tldr: Only selected levels of a finely recorded exposure may define meaningful interventions. Under positive-probability random assignment and exclusion restricted to those levels, the full categorical instrumental-variable model has an exact quotient: the sharp law of the target potential-outcome vector is the image of a reduced response simplex that keeps target outcome cells and one off-target mass per arm. An explicit boundary-safe right inverse proves independence from the number and labels of off-target categories. Conditional on fixed finite arm counts, the same quotient factors the experiment and yields equality of nuisance-minimax decision values for convex loss through a finite-fiber kernel. It also supports a finite-sample method-of-types confidence region for the entire sharp set whose calibration is independent of \(|\mathcal C|\). A compatible-fiber Hoffman theorem controls excess width, a local lower bound certifies the root-\(n\) regular-face rate, and the exact kink frontier remains the central open question.

project_justification.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander's target-level coarsening calculations stop at specified low cardinalities, whereas Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson's adjacent arbitrary-cardinality theory assumes excluded potential outcomes for every exposure category and identifies the larger all-exposure law. Full-alphabet inference consequently confounds scientific target dimension with arbitrary recording detail.
project_justification.niche: The relevant model has common potential outcomes only on \(\mathcal T\), saturated \(R_{c,z}\) on \(\mathcal C\), and asks for the whole law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\) rather than a single selected endpoint.
project_justification.fill: The quotient and its right inverse give sharp identification; the product likelihood and finite-fiber convexification give the exact nuisance-minimax comparison in the conditional finite-count experiment; reduced KL projection gives kink-robust finite-sample coverage; and polyhedral stability converts its radius to a target-set excess bound.

body.related_work: The field-tier comparison has two distinct axes. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander \cite{GabrielSachsSjolander2025} distinguish meaningful target levels from ill-defined or contaminated levels and prove specified low-cardinality target-contrast results; Theorem 1 strictly extends that line to arbitrary finite \(m,\mathcal T,\mathcal C\), the complete law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\), and a boundary-safe right inverse. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson \cite{SongGuoChanRichardson2024} are the adjacent arbitrary-cardinality fully excluded benchmark: their common-response restriction \(R_{c,z}=R_c\) is strictly contained in the saturated off-target class for \(m\ge2\) and nonempty \(\mathcal C\). Song et al. identify the larger all-exposure potential-outcome law under stronger exclusion, while Theorem 1 identifies the target marginal after exclusion is relaxed on \(\mathcal C\); Proposition 1 certifies that this relaxation changes target bounds. Their KL construction informs the reduced confidence region, but no equality between their projected set and \(\Theta(s)\) is claimed. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel \cite{SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2023} provide the response-function incidence machinery adapted by the quotient proof. Guo and Richardson \cite{GuoRichardson2021} provide the alphabet-generic relative-entropy concentration tool. Blackwell \cite{Blackwell1953} supplies the experiment-comparison template, while the unknown allocation kernel forces the nuisance-minimax rather than pointwise comparison. Hoffman \cite{Hoffman1952} and Li \cite{Li1993} supply generic polyhedral error-bound tools used to obtain the reduced causal modulus. Levis et al. \cite{LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025} and Gafarov \cite{Gafarov2025} locate the active-facet inference problem but do not solve the target-specific kink frontier. Boushehrian et al. \cite{BoushehrianBadriAkbariKiyavash2026} show why exponential dependence on substantive support can remain even after irrelevant off-target cardinality is removed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The method-of-types radius is deliberately elementary and can be conservatively larger than the polynomial Chernoff calibration of Guo and Richardson. The novelty is the quotient that permits either calibration on \(d=2|\mathcal T|+1\) cells, not a new multinomial tail inequality. Song et al. remain an adjacent stronger-assumption benchmark for a larger all-exposure estimand; no equality with their projected set is asserted. The nuisance-minimax comparison is confined to the finite count experiment conditional on fixed arm counts; it does not assert a pointwise comparison at arbitrary \(\eta\) or an abstract infinite-sample-space theorem. The exact smallest Hoffman constant and the nonregular kink rate are not presupposed.
body.honest_scope: The equality of full and reduced identified images, the right inverse, the finite-count nuisance-minimax theorem, finite-sample whole-set coverage, the finite Hoffman certificate, and the regular-face lower bound are theorem obligations. The condition \(\lambda_z>0\) only makes the population conditional laws \(p_z\) and \(s_z\) well defined; it imposes no restriction on response types, feasible fibers, or the right-inverse equality. The separate condition \(n_z\ge1\) concerns the realized conditional sampling experiment. The minimax equality uses finite fibers and convexity only, so it requires neither closedness of \(\mathcal A\) nor an integrability assumption. The exact face-by-face minimax law and an adaptive attaining procedure at dual ties remain open. When \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\), \(m=2\), and \(|\mathcal T|=2\), the construction reduces to the classical Balke--Pearl response-type program.
